# WheelOrder — what each wheel adds when wheels arrive in order

**Generated file — do not edit.** Regenerated by `python scripts/graph.py`.

**Status:** proved in Lean

Bringing wheels in one at a time, the positions a wheel blocks for the first time equal the open positions left by every earlier wheel times the full size of every later wheel. Separately, from any 6n±1 position, the next number with a chosen last digit is reached in the raw digit distance or at most one further step of 10.

## Published sources

Published work this node rests on or relates to; each entry says how.

- [Wheel factorization (Wikipedia)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wheel_factorization) — the computing method of skipping blocked positions; this node's first-blocking count is the network's own form of it, and the digit-distance claims are original here

## Claims

<a id="wheel_marginal_new_formula"></a>
### `wheel_marginal_new_formula`

The positions a wheel blocks first equal the open positions of the earlier wheels times the sizes of the later ones.

```lean
/-- **The marginal contribution of one wheel.** For distinct primes `before`
brought in first, then the prime `p`, then any further moduli `after`: the
positions of the full cycle that `p` blocks while every earlier wheel leaves
them open number exactly the product of (each earlier wheel size minus one),
times the product of the later moduli. -/
def wheel_marginal_new_formula : Prop :=
  ∀ (before : List Nat) (p : Nat) (after : List Nat),
    p.Prime → (∀ q ∈ before, q.Prime) → before.Nodup → p ∉ before →
      ((Finset.range ((before ++ p :: after).prod)).filter
          (fun x => p ∣ x ∧ ∀ q ∈ before, ¬ q ∣ x)).card
        = (before.map (· - 1)).prod * after.prod
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.WheelOrder.wheel_marginal_new_formula_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/WheelOrder.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/WheelOrder.lean)

<a id="prime_gt_five_digit_ok"></a>
### `prime_gt_five_digit_ok`

Every prime above 5 ends in 1, 3, 7 or 9.

```lean
/-- **Every prime above 5 passes the last-digit wheel.** -/
def prime_gt_five_digit_ok : Prop :=
  ∀ p : Nat, p.Prime → p > 5 → digit_ok p = true
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.WheelOrder.prime_gt_five_digit_ok_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/WheelOrder.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/WheelOrder.lean)

<a id="wheel_gap_floor"></a>
### `wheel_gap_floor`

From any 6n+-1 position, the next number with a chosen last digit is the raw digit distance away, or 10 more.

```lean
/-- **The wheel-gap floor.** From any number on the 6n±1 wheel, stepping
forward by the raw last-digit distance to a target digit 1, 3, 7 or 9 lands
on the wheel again, or does after exactly one further step of 10. -/
def wheel_gap_floor : Prop :=
  ∀ n b : Nat, is_candidate n = true → (b = 1 ∨ b = 3 ∨ b = 7 ∨ b = 9) →
    is_candidate (n + digit_gap (n % 10) b) = true ∨
      is_candidate (n + digit_gap (n % 10) b + 10) = true
```

**Rests on:** no other node (Mathlib and the Vocabulary only)

**Proof:** `RNS.WheelOrder.wheel_gap_floor_holds` in [`RNSSolutions/WheelOrder.lean`](../../RNSSolutions/WheelOrder.lean)
